intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Begin your mornings with a guided yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud. This gentle hilltop trail offers breathtaking views of lush green valleys and is ideal for yoga practitioners of all levels. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, this is best scheduled from Day 2 onward. Many local instructors offer small-group sessions right on the ridge at dawn, combining movement with nature immersion. Staying in central Ubud means you can walk to the trailhead within minutes, maximizing your time.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Seminyak Beach is one of Bali's most celebrated stretches of golden sand, known for its reliable waves and vibrant sunset atmosphere. Book a beginner-to-intermediate surf lesson with a certified local instructor in the late afternoon, then stay to watch the legendary Bali sunset. Choosing accommodation in Seminyak or Kerobokan puts you within walking distance, eliminating long transfers and making this a seamless daily ritual during your 13-day stay.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Local Market Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Balinese culinary culture with a hands-on cooking class that begins at a traditional morning market in Ubud. Your guide walks you through selecting fresh spices, tropical fruits, and local ingredients before heading to a family compound to cook authentic dishes like Nasi Goreng, Satay Lilit, and Lawar. This experience is culturally rich, delicious, and perfectly timed for a mid-morning start — ideal after a Day 1 rest following your late arrival.

experiences.name: Tirta Empul Temple Purification Ritual
experiences.description: Visit the sacred Tirta Empul water temple, where Balinese Hindus perform melukat — a traditional purification ritual in holy spring water. Respectfully participate in the ritual under the guidance of a local priest or cultural guide. This deeply spiritual experience connects you to Bali's living Hindu culture and pairs beautifully with your yoga journey. The temple is located near Ubud, making it easily accessible if you stay centrally. Avoid scheduling this on Day 1 given your late arrival.

experiences.name: Yin Yoga & Sound Healing Retreat Day
experiences.description: Dedicate one full day to a deeply restorative Yin Yoga and Sound Healing session at one of Ubud's renowned wellness centers such as The Yoga Barn or Radiantly Alive. These studios offer drop-in full-day passes combining multiple classes, sound bath ceremonies with singing bowls, and guided meditation. Located in the heart of Ubud, this experience is perfectly aligned with your yoga interest and budget. Staying in central Ubud means zero commute, leaving you fully refreshed for the rest of your 13-day journey.
experiences.location: The Yoga Barn area, Central Ubud

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a pre-booked shared shuttle or Grab app ride from the airport to Ubud Boutique Stay (approx. 1.5–2 hrs, ~IDR 100,000–150,000). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along Monkey Forest Road to get your bearings and soak in the lush Ubud atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Ubud Night Market (Pasar Senggol) near Ubud Palace for an authentic introduction to Balinese street food and local crafts. Watch the free Kecak or Legong dance performance at Ubud Palace if timing aligns (usually starts around 19:30, tickets ~IDR 100,000).

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a warung near the hotel upon arrival — try nasi campur for ~IDR 25,000.
meals.dinner: Ubud Night Market stalls — try satay, martabak, and fresh coconut for under IDR 50,000 total.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport (avoid airport exchange booths for large amounts — use ATMs in Ubud for better rates). Save Grab app offline or download Maps.me for navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a free sunrise yoga session at one of Ubud's community parks or a drop-in class at a budget studio like Yoga Barn (drop-in ~IDR 120,000). Afterward, walk the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk — a scenic 2 km trail through green hillside and rice paddies, completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (entry ~IDR 80,000) — wander among ancient temples and hundreds of Balinese long-tailed macaques. Stroll through Ubud Art Market (Pasar Seni) to browse handmade crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs at negotiable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Balinese cooking class at a budget community kitchen (some run for ~IDR 150,000–200,000 including market visit). Alternatively, dine at a local warung and head to Pura Taman Saraswati temple for the free lotus pond view.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or banana pancakes at a local café near the hotel — ~IDR 30,000–40,000.
meals.lunch: Warung Ibu Oka or a nearby warung for babi guling (suckling pig) or nasi goreng — ~IDR 35,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling Pak Malen or a cooking class meal — budget ~IDR 50,000–60,000.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the ridge walk. Bring a light rain jacket as afternoon showers are possible even in July.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the breathtaking Tegallalang Rice Terraces (entry ~IDR 15,000 donation). Arrive before 9:00 to beat crowds and enjoy the golden morning light over the UNESCO-listed terraced fields. Optional: try the famous rice terrace swing for photos (~IDR 100,000–150,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Tirta Empul Temple (entry ~IDR 50,000), one of Bali's most sacred water temples where locals perform purification rituals in holy spring water. Respectful observers are welcome. Afterward, stop at Gunung Kawi — an 11th-century royal tomb complex carved into a cliff (~IDR 50,000 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud and enjoy a relaxing yin yoga or meditation class at a budget studio (~IDR 100,000 drop-in). Wind down with dinner at a rooftop warung overlooking the jungle.

meals.breakfast: Nasi jinggo (small rice parcels) from a street vendor — ~IDR 10,000–15,000 each.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or local warung near Tegallalang — nasi campur ~IDR 25,000–30,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Sopa (vegetarian-friendly, budget-friendly) in Ubud — ~IDR 50,000–70,000.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a sarong for temple visits (often provided at entrance for a small fee or free). Stay hydrated — carry a refillable water bottle to save money and reduce plastic waste.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning scooter rental (IDR 60,000–80,000/day from local shops) or shared van to Mount Batur for a sunrise trek. The hike takes about 2 hours up and rewards you with panoramic views of the volcanic crater lake. Local guide fee ~IDR 150,000–200,000 (mandatory).
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the natural hot springs at the base of Mount Batur (Toya Devasya or budget options ~IDR 50,000–100,000) to rest your legs. Drive back toward Ubud via Kintamani for scenic lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recovery evening — gentle stretching or restorative yoga back at the hotel or studio. Explore Ubud's Jalan Dewi Sita street for local boutiques and art galleries (free to browse).

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast cooked at the summit or brought from the hotel — budget IDR 20,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Kintamani overlooking Lake Batur — nasi goreng or mie goreng ~IDR 30,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Teges or similar local spot in Ubud — budget ~IDR 45,000–60,000.

day_by_day.notes: Start the Mount Batur trek by 4:00 AM. Bring a torch/headlamp, warm layer for the summit, and snacks. Book guide the evening before through your hotel to save on agency fees.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the beach! Rent a scooter or take a shared bemo to Sanur Beach (about 40 mins from Ubud). Sanur is calm, clean, and far less crowded than Kuta — perfect for a peaceful morning swim and beach yoga on the sand (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the scenic Sanur beachfront promenade (free, about 4 km). Rent a paddleboard or kayak (~IDR 50,000–80,000/hour) and enjoy the warm Indian Ocean. Browse the local art market stalls along the path.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the stunning Sanur sunset from the beach — one of the best sunset spots on the island. Head back to Ubud via shared transport or Grab. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Fruit salad and coffee at a beachfront warung in Sanur — ~IDR 30,000–40,000.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or seafood at a beachside warung — ~IDR 40,000–60,000.
meals.dinner: Local warung in Ubud upon return — nasi campur ~IDR 30,000–40,000.

day_by_day.notes: Sanur has calm waters ideal for beginners. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a reusable bag. The shared bemo from Ubud to Sanur costs ~IDR 20,000–30,000 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a morning Hatha yoga class at a budget studio in Ubud (~IDR 100,000 drop-in). Afterward, visit Pura Dalem Ubud or Pura Puseh Ubud — free or small donation — to experience authentic Balinese Hindu temple architecture without tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ubud Traditional Art Museum (Museum Puri Lukisan, entry ~IDR 75,000) to learn about Balinese painting traditions. Then take a free self-guided walk through the Penestanan village — a quiet artists' enclave with rice fields and traditional homes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Barong and Kris dance performance at Batubulan or a local cultural center (~IDR 100,000). This traditional dance depicts the eternal battle between good (Barong) and evil (Rangda) and is a must-see cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Jamu (traditional herbal drink) and banana fritters from a street vendor — ~IDR 15,000.
meals.lunch: Warung Biah Biah — authentic Balinese home cooking ~IDR 35,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Night market or local warung — budget ~IDR 40,000–50,000.

day_by_day.notes: Many temples offer free entry with a sarong; always dress modestly. Check the Balinese calendar — if there's a local ceremony, attending respectfully is free and unforgettable.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Seminyak Beach — rent a scooter or take a Grab. Seminyak offers a livelier beach scene with great surf watching. Walk along the beach from Seminyak toward Petitenget for a beautiful stretch of golden sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Petitenget Temple (Pura Petitenget) — a sacred sea temple perched near the beach (free with sarong). Explore the Seminyak area's colorful street murals and boutique shops (window shopping is free!). Cool off with a dip in the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the legendary Seminyak sunset — one of Bali's most spectacular. Watch from the beach or a budget beach club with a single drink purchase. Drive back to Ubud by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel or a café in Ubud before departing — ~IDR 25,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Seminyak Beach — grilled corn, satay, fresh juice ~IDR 40,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Eat before leaving Seminyak — try a local warung on Jalan Raya Seminyak ~IDR 45,000–60,000.

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is about 1.5 hrs from Ubud. Leave by 8:30 AM to make the most of the day. Scooter rental is the most economical option (~IDR 70,000/day).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and slow morning — enjoy a gentle sunrise meditation or pranayama session in your hotel garden or a nearby rice field path. Then visit the Ubud Organic Market at Jalan Raya Ubud (open Wednesday and Saturday mornings) for fresh tropical fruits and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free self-guided cycling or walking tour of Ubud's surrounding villages — Mas (woodcarving), Celuk (silversmithing), and Batubulan (stone carving). Watch artisans at work in their open workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a budget traditional Balinese massage at a local spa (60 min ~IDR 80,000–120,000). Finish the day with a quiet dinner and journaling session.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit, tempe, and local coffee from the organic market — ~IDR 20,000–30,000.
meals.lunch: Warung in Mas or Celuk village — simple rice dish ~IDR 25,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Mendez or similar in Ubud — budget ~IDR 40,000–55,000.

day_by_day.notes: Wednesday and Saturday are organic market days — arrive by 8:00 AM for the best selection. Cycling rentals available near the hotel for ~IDR 50,000/day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Nusa Dua / Tanjung Benoa area for a beach day with a different vibe. Take a Grab or shared shuttle (~IDR 100,000–150,000 one way). Enjoy the calm, turquoise waters and white sand beaches — ideal for snorkeling from the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent basic snorkel gear (~IDR 30,000–50,000) and explore the shallow reef. Alternatively, join a budget banana boat or parasailing session if feeling adventurous (~IDR 100,000–150,000). Stroll the Nusa Dua beach boardwalk for free.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Kuta or Legian for the evening — explore the famous Kuta Beach at sunset (free). Browse Kuta's busy street market for souvenirs at bargain prices. Return to Ubud by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Eaten at hotel or a quick stop en route — ~IDR 25,000.
meals.lunch: Beachside warung in Tanjung Benoa — fresh seafood rice box ~IDR 40,000–55,000.
meals.dinner: Kuta street food — nasi goreng, satay, fresh coconut ~IDR 35,000–50,000.

day_by_day.notes: Nusa Dua's public beach areas are free — avoid the resort-only sections. The snorkeling near the reef at Tanjung Benoa is best in the morning before afternoon boat traffic increases.

day_by_day.morning: Morning vinyasa yoga class at a local Ubud studio (~IDR 100,000). Afterward, visit Pura Tirta Empul again for a deeper experience — consider participating in the melukat (holy water purification) ritual yourself (respectful participation is welcome, small offering ~IDR 30,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave Temple, entry ~IDR 50,000) — a 9th-century archaeological site with a carved cave entrance, bathing pools, and meditation niches. Combine with a walk to the nearby Yeh Pulu rock reliefs (small donation).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk to the Campuhan Ridge for the second time — the light is different every evening. End the night with a traditional Balinese dinner at a community warung.

meals.breakfast: Bubur ayam (rice porridge) from a local street cart — ~IDR 15,000–20,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Goa Gajah — nasi campur ~IDR 30,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Pulau Kelapa or similar in Ubud — ~IDR 50,000–65,000.

day_by_day.notes: Goa Gajah and Yeh Pulu are within walking distance of each other — combine both in one afternoon. Wear sturdy sandals as paths can be uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Full day trip to Amed Beach on Bali's northeast coast — one of the island's best-kept secrets for budget travelers. Hire a scooter or join a shared day tour (~IDR 200,000–300,000 including transport). Amed offers black volcanic sand beaches and world-class snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel over the famous USAT Liberty shipwreck at nearby Tulamben (gear rental ~IDR 50,000, entry ~IDR 20,000). The shallow wreck is teeming with colorful marine life and accessible to beginners. Relax on Amed's quiet beach afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Mount Agung from Amed's shoreline — a dramatic and unforgettable view. Begin the drive back to Ubud (about 2 hours), arriving by 20:30.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at hotel before early departure — ~IDR 20,000–30,000.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a beachfront warung in Amed — ~IDR 45,000–60,000.
meals.dinner: Warung in Ubud upon return — keep it simple, budget ~IDR 35,000–45,000.

day_by_day.notes: Leave Ubud by 7:00 AM for Amed. The drive is scenic but winding — scooter riders should be experienced. Alternatively, book a budget day tour through your hotel for ~IDR 300,000 including driver.

day_by_day.morning: Final full yoga day — attend a 2-hour Ashtanga or Kundalini class at Yoga Barn or a similar studio (~IDR 120,000–150,000). Treat this as a mindful, intentional practice to reflect on your journey. Afterward, journal in a rice field café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do your souvenir shopping at Ubud Art Market — bargain for batik fabric, silver jewelry, wooden carvings, and handmade offerings. Budget ~IDR 100,000–200,000 for gifts. Then visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum (entry ~IDR 80,000) — a stunning artist's villa perched above the Campuhan River.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — splurge a little on your last full evening. Watch a final Kecak fire dance performance at Pura Uluwatu if you can arrange transport (~IDR 100,000 entry, transport ~IDR 150,000 return).

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl or full Balinese breakfast at a favorite café — ~IDR 40,000–55,000.
meals.lunch: Warung Biah Biah revisit or a new local spot — ~IDR 40,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Warung Nia or Locavore To Go (budget line of the acclaimed restaurant) — ~IDR 80,000–120,000.

day_by_day.notes: The Kecak dance at Uluwatu is one of Bali's most iconic performances — highly recommended for the last evening. Book transport through your hotel in the afternoon to save on last-minute costs.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise meditation or a short walk through the rice paddies near the hotel. Pack and check out. Leave a small tip for hotel staff as a gesture of appreciation (IDR 50,000–100,000 is meaningful and appreciated).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, stop at a final café in Ubud for a last sip of Balinese kopi tubruk (traditional coffee). Travel to Ngurah Rai Airport via Grab or pre-booked shuttle (~IDR 150,000–200,000 from Ubud). Allow 2–2.5 hours for the journey plus check-in time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with incredible memories, a recharged spirit, and a deeper love for yoga, beaches, and Balinese culture.

meals.breakfast: Final nasi goreng or fruit plate at a favorite Ubud warung — ~IDR 25,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or a final warung stop en route — ~IDR 20,000–30,000.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight details the night before. Bali's airport can be busy — arrive at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Keep some IDR for airport snacks or last-minute purchases. Total estimated daily budget: IDR 200,000–400,000 (~$13–$26 USD) per day excluding accommodation.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport transfer to Ubud Boutique Stay (~1.5 hrs). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along Monkey Forest Road to get oriented. Visit the iconic Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary for a relaxed first Bali experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ubud's vibrant night market on Jalan Dewi Sita. Browse local crafts and soak in the atmosphere of your new home base.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Warung Ibu Oka near the airport or a roadside warung during your transfer
meals.dinner: Locavore NXT on Jalan Dewi Sita — mid-range farm-to-table Indonesian cuisine with a relaxed vibe

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag is real. Hydrate well and avoid heavy scheduling. Exchange some cash at the airport or a reputable money changer in Ubud.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Bali mornings right with a sunrise yoga class at The Yoga Barn, one of Ubud's most celebrated yoga studios. Choose from Hatha or Vinyasa flow sessions starting at 07:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Tegallalang Rice Terraces (about 20 min north of Ubud). Walk the terraced paths, take in the lush views, and optionally try the famous rice terrace swing. Explore the artisan shops along the roadside.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud temple — an unmissable cultural spectacle held at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Café Wayan on Monkey Forest Road — classic Balinese breakfast with banana pancakes and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Warung Bodag Maliah at Tegallalang — local warung with nasi campur and scenic rice terrace views
meals.dinner: Bridges Bali Restaurant — mid-range dining with Indonesian fusion cuisine and lovely jungle gorge views

day_by_day.notes: Book The Yoga Barn class in advance online. The Kecak dance tickets can be purchased at the temple gate — arrive 30 minutes early for good seats.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and pranayama session at Radiantly Alive Yoga Studio in central Ubud. Follow with a walk through the Ubud Palace grounds (Puri Saren Agung).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud Art Market (Pasar Seni Ubud) for local batik, crafts, and souvenirs. Then visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum to appreciate the flamboyant art of Don Antonio Blanco.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Balinese massage at one of Ubud's reputable mid-range spas, such as Karsa Spa or Taksu Spa, to recover and relax.

meals.breakfast: Seniman Coffee Studio — excellent single-origin Balinese coffee with avocado toast
meals.lunch: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka — legendary Balinese suckling pig, a must-try local institution
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique — splurge-worthy garden dining with creative Indonesian-French cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Ubud Art Market is best visited in the morning when it's less crowded. Bargaining is expected and part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike to Mount Batur for sunrise (depart hotel by 02:00 AM). Trek with a licensed guide (~2 hrs up) and reach the summit by sunrise around 05:30. Breathtaking views over Lake Batur and Mount Agung.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ubud by mid-morning. Rest and recover at the hotel. Optional: soak in natural hot springs at Toya Devasya near Kintamani on the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle restorative yoga session at The Yoga Barn to ease tired muscles from the hike.

meals.breakfast: Simple snacks and coffee provided by your guide at the Mount Batur summit
meals.lunch: Kintamani-area warung with panoramic lake views — try local corn and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Room service or light meal at the hotel — keep it easy after a big day

day_by_day.notes: Book a licensed Batur trekking guide in advance (approx. IDR 350,000–500,000 per person). Bring warm layers, a headlamp, and sturdy shoes. This is a long day — consider it your adventure day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tirta Empul Temple — a sacred Hindu water temple where locals and visitors participate in a traditional purification ritual (melukat). Respectful dress required (sarong provided).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Gunung Kawi Temple complex, one of Bali's oldest and most impressive archaeological sites carved into a rock cliff. Walk through lush rice paddies to reach the site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Visit the Ubud night scene — enjoy live jazz at Laughing Buddha Bar or a quiet drink at Room4Dessert.

meals.breakfast: Bali Buda Café — healthy smoothie bowls and organic options
meals.lunch: Warung near Tirta Empul — simple nasi goreng or mie goreng at local prices
meals.dinner: Hujan Locale — contemporary Indonesian cuisine with a focus on regional flavors from across the archipelago

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong at both temples (available to borrow/rent at the entrance). Tirta Empul can be crowded — arrive early for a more serene experience. Bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to Seminyak (~1.5 hrs). Check into a mid-range beachside guesthouse or boutique hotel. Head straight to Seminyak Beach for a morning swim and beach walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a sun lounger at a beach club such as Ku De Ta or Potato Head Beach Club. Enjoy the warm July weather, ocean views, and a refreshing cocktail.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Seminyak sunset from the beach — one of the best in Bali. Explore Seminyak's boutique shopping strip on Jalan Kayu Aya.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Revolver Espresso — famous for specialty coffee and toasties
meals.lunch: La Lucciola Restaurant — beachfront dining with Italian-Indonesian fusion and stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Metis Restaurant — elegant French-Mediterranean cuisine in a beautiful garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is a change of pace from Ubud — more beach, more buzz. The beach clubs can be pricey but you can enjoy the vibe with just a drink minimum spend. Keep valuables secure on the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga session on Seminyak Beach (many instructors offer outdoor classes) or join a class at Desa Seni Yoga Village nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tanah Lot Temple (~30 min from Seminyak) — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop. Explore the surrounding coastal cliffs and temple grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seminyak for dinner and an evening exploring the lively Eat Street (Jalan Laksmana) restaurant row.

meals.breakfast: Nook Bali — cozy café with rice field views and healthy breakfast options
meals.lunch: Warung near Tanah Lot — local food stalls with affordable Balinese staples
meals.dinner: Sarong Restaurant — award-winning Asian tapas with bold flavors in a beautiful setting

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is best visited in the late afternoon for the sunset view over the temple. Entry fee applies (~IDR 60,000). The area around the temple has many souvenir stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Canggu (~20 min from Seminyak). Explore the hip neighborhood and join a morning surf lesson at one of Batu Bolong Beach's many surf schools — great for beginners and intermediates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Echo Beach, Canggu's famous black sand beach. Enjoy the laid-back vibe, watch local surfers, and explore the trendy cafés and warungs along the beachfront.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Canggu's vibrant social scene — visit Old Man's Bar for live music and a fun atmosphere, or enjoy a sunset beer at The Lawn beach club.

meals.breakfast: Betelnut Café in Seminyak before departing — excellent smoothie bowls and eggs
meals.lunch: Warung Dandelion at Echo Beach — casual beachside dining with fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Crate Café or Peloton Supershop — Canggu's beloved plant-based and healthy eateries

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons in Canggu run approximately IDR 150,000–250,000 per hour including board and instructor. Rip currents can be strong — always surf with a guide if you're a beginner.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer south to the Bukit Peninsula (~45 min). Visit the spectacular Uluwatu Temple perched 70m above the Indian Ocean on dramatic sea cliffs. Watch for mischievous monkeys!
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Padang Padang Beach — one of Bali's most beautiful and intimate beaches. Swim, snorkel, and relax on this sheltered white sand cove.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Uluwatu for the famous Kecak fire dance performance at the cliff-top amphitheater at sunset — a more dramatic setting than Ubud's version.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab food from a warung in Seminyak before departing
meals.lunch: Single Fin Restaurant at Uluwatu — stunning clifftop ocean views with burgers and Indonesian dishes
meals.dinner: Warung at Jimbaran Bay — fresh grilled seafood on the beach, a classic Bali experience

day_by_day.notes: Secure your belongings tightly at Uluwatu — monkeys are known to snatch glasses, phones, and bags. Wear a sarong at the temple. Book Kecak dance tickets in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nusa Dua area — start with a morning yoga session on the beach or at a resort yoga pavilion. Then explore the Garuda Wisnu Kencana Cultural Park (GWK) with its massive iconic statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Nusa Dua Beach — calm, turquoise water ideal for swimming. Try water sports such as parasailing or jet skiing from the beach operators.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seminyak for your final evening in the south. Treat yourself to a Balinese spa treatment at Jari Menari or Prana Spa.

meals.breakfast: Swept Away at COMO Uma Canggu or a beachside café in Nusa Dua
meals.lunch: Bumbu Bali Restaurant — authentic Balinese royal cuisine in a beautiful garden setting
meals.dinner: Mama San — stylish colonial-era restaurant with creative Asian cuisine in Seminyak

day_by_day.notes: GWK Cultural Park entry is approximately IDR 125,000. Nusa Dua is generally calmer and more resort-oriented — a nice contrast to the Seminyak buzz.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer back to Ubud (~1.5 hrs). On the way, stop at Penglipuran Village — one of Bali's cleanest and most traditional villages with beautifully maintained bamboo gates and temple courtyards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tirta Gangga Water Palace, a stunning royal garden with tiered fountains, stone carvings, and koi-filled pools. Walk through the surrounding rice terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Attend a traditional Legong dance performance at Ubud Palace — a graceful and intricate Balinese dance form.

meals.breakfast: Roadside warung breakfast during transfer — nasi jinggo (small banana leaf rice packets) is a local favorite
meals.lunch: Local warung near Tirta Gangga — fresh lawar and sate lilit
meals.dinner: Naughty Nuri's Warung — famous for BBQ ribs and cold Bintang beer, a Ubud institution

day_by_day.notes: Penglipuran Village charges a small entry fee (~IDR 30,000). Tirta Gangga is about 1.5 hrs from Ubud — consider combining both stops on the journey back to make the most of the drive.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning yoga class at The Yoga Barn — choose a deeper practice such as Yin Yoga or a 90-minute Ashtanga session. Reflect on your Bali journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Campuhan Ridge Walk — a scenic 2 km trail through lush jungle and along a ridge with sweeping valley views, right from the edge of Ubud town. Perfect in the warm July weather.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Balinese cooking class in the evening — learn to make traditional dishes such as sate, lawar, and black rice pudding. Komaneka Cooking Class or Paon Bali are excellent options.

meals.breakfast: Clear Café Ubud — organic, health-conscious breakfast with beautiful garden seating
meals.lunch: Warung Teges on the way back from the ridge walk — simple and delicious local food
meals.dinner: Eat what you cook at the cooking class — a delicious and memorable final dinner experience

day_by_day.notes: The Campuhan Ridge Walk is best done before 09:00 or after 16:00 to avoid midday heat. Cooking classes run approximately IDR 350,000–500,000 per person and usually include a market tour.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle final morning — pack up and enjoy a slow breakfast. Take a last stroll through Ubud's streets, visit your favorite café, and pick up any last-minute souvenirs from the art market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Ngurah Rai International Airport (~1.5–2 hrs depending on traffic). Allow extra time for Bali's unpredictable traffic. Check in and prepare for your flight home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry your memories, your yoga practice, and perhaps a bottle of local Arak or Balinese coffee home with you.

meals.breakfast: Kafe Batan Waru — lovely final Balinese breakfast with jamu (herbal tonic) and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport — Puri Selera at the international terminal serves decent Indonesian food
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Bali traffic can be severe — depart for the airport at least 3 hours before your flight. Double-check your luggage for any restricted items (certain wooden crafts and plant products may require customs declarations). Consider a final offering at a small temple to honor Balinese tradition.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Ubud Boutique Stay in Ubud (approx. 1.5 hrs). Check in, settle into your luxury villa, and enjoy a welcome drink and traditional Balinese foot ritual offered by the resort. Take a leisurely stroll through the boutique property gardens to acclimatize.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle orientation walk through central Ubud — explore Jalan Hanoman and the surrounding lanes at dusk. Visit the iconic Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) exterior for an atmospheric first glimpse of Balinese culture.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Locavore, Ubud's celebrated farm-to-table fine dining restaurant. Opt for the tasting menu featuring hyper-local Balinese ingredients with expert wine pairings. Reservation essential — confirm in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Request early check-in if possible. Ensure hotel arranges private airport transfer in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session at your boutique stay or at a premium Ubud studio such as The Yoga Barn — choose a Hatha or Vinyasa class with views over the jungle canopy. Follow with a nourishing smoothie bowl at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural walk through Ubud's famous Monkey Forest (Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary), then visit local artisan workshops in Mas village — watch master woodcarvers and painters at work. Stop at a premium gallery to browse authentic Balinese art.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Ubud Palace — one of Bali's most mesmerizing cultural spectacles, typically held at sunset.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast — freshly pressed juices, tropical fruit platters, eggs Benedict with local herbs, and Balinese coffee at the hotel's garden terrace.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique — enjoy a leisurely set lunch surrounded by tropical gardens, featuring French-influenced cuisine with Balinese ingredients.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bridges Bali — a dramatic clifftop restaurant overlooking the Campuhan River, offering modern European cuisine with an exceptional wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Book Kecak performance tickets in advance. Bring a light shawl for temple visits. Yoga Barn classes book up quickly — reserve online the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga and meditation session arranged by the hotel in a secluded jungle pavilion or rice terrace setting. Follow with a traditional Balinese healing breakfast — jamu (herbal tonic), black rice porridge, and fresh tropical fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided trek through the iconic Tegalalang Rice Terraces — explore the UNESCO-recognized subak irrigation landscape. Continue to Tirta Empul Holy Spring Temple for a purification ritual experience (melukat) guided by a local priest.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a 90-minute Balinese massage and spa treatment at the boutique stay's luxury spa — choose from hot stone therapy, traditional boreh body wrap, or a couple's ritual.

meals.breakfast: In-resort Balinese healing breakfast as described above.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the rice terraces — arrange with the hotel in advance for a curated gourmet basket with local delicacies, cold-pressed juices, and artisan cheeses.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Swept Away at COMO Shambhala Estate — an open-air riverside restaurant offering organic, health-focused cuisine in a breathtaking jungle setting.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable trekking sandals for the rice terrace walk. Bring a sarong for the temple visit — one will also be provided on-site. The purification ritual requires modest dress.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin Yoga or Restorative Yoga class at The Yoga Barn, followed by a guided meditation session. Enjoy post-class herbal tea and a raw food snack at the Yoga Barn café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Ubud's cultural landmarks — Ubud Museum (Puri Lukisan), Blanco Renaissance Museum, and the royal Saraswati Temple with its stunning lotus pond. Visit a premium batik and ikat textile studio for a hands-on weaving demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Room4Dessert or a rooftop bar in central Ubud, followed by an evening at leisure to explore Ubud's vibrant night market (Pasar Malam) for local snacks and handcrafted souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — avocado toast on sourdough, poached eggs, granola with coconut yogurt, and fresh Bali coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hujan Locale — a stylish, award-winning restaurant celebrating Indonesian regional cuisine with a modern twist and curated cocktail menu.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alaya Resort's Plantation restaurant — rooftop dining with panoramic views over Ubud's rooftops, serving contemporary Indonesian cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Puri Lukisan and Blanco Museum charge entry fees — arrange private guide through the hotel concierge for an enriched experience. Night market is casual but vibrant.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise hike to Mount Batur (Kintamani) — depart by 03:30 from Ubud for a guided 2-hour trek to the summit (1,717m). Watch the sunrise above the clouds and over Lake Batur — a truly spectacular Bali highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and soak in natural hot springs at Toya Devasya Hot Springs Resort — enjoy thermal pools with views of the volcano and lake. Return to Ubud by early afternoon for rest and recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — enjoy a private villa dinner or in-room dining experience with a curated menu and a bottle of fine wine selected by the hotel sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-hike snack pack arranged by the hotel (energy bars, bananas, thermos of Balinese coffee). Post-hike breakfast at the hot springs resort — nasi goreng, fresh fruit, and coconut water.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic warung (traditional restaurant) in Kintamani overlooking the caldera — try local Balinese babi guling (suckling pig) or vegetarian options.
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining experience at Ubud Boutique Stay — curated 4-course menu with wine pairing, served by a dedicated butler under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Mount Batur hike requires a licensed guide — arrange through the hotel concierge at least 2 days in advance. Bring warm layers for the summit (temperatures can drop to 10°C before dawn). Sturdy closed-toe shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — gentle restorative yoga session at the hotel, followed by a Balinese traditional breakfast in bed or on your private terrace. Optional: book a 60-minute aromatherapy massage at the spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at a premium Ubud culinary school (e.g., Paon Bali or Casa Luna Cooking School) — learn to prepare 5–6 traditional Balinese dishes from scratch, including market shopping for fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Campuhan Ridge — a scenic jungle ridge trail with sweeping views over Ubud's green valleys, ideal at golden hour. Return to the resort for a candlelit dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room or terrace breakfast — Balinese black rice pudding, tropical fruit, freshly baked pastries, and Kintamani single-origin coffee.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during your cooking class as part of the culinary experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ku De Ta Ubud or Merah Putih — sophisticated Indonesian fine dining with a vibrant ambiance and creative cocktail program.

day_by_day.notes: Campuhan Ridge walk is best done 30–45 minutes before sunset. Wear comfortable shoes and bring insect repellent. Cooking class typically lasts 4–5 hours including the market visit.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Seminyak/Canggu beach area — private chauffeured transfer (approx. 1.5 hrs). Morning beach yoga session on the sand at a premium beach club (e.g., Finns Beach Club or Deus Ex Machina) with a certified instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at Potato Head Beach Club or Ku De Ta Seminyak — relax on premium sun loungers, swim in the infinity pool overlooking the Indian Ocean, and enjoy curated cocktails and light bites. Optional: surf lesson for beginners on Seminyak's gentle waves.
day_by_day.evening: Watch Bali's legendary sunset from the beach at Seminyak — one of the finest sunsets in Southeast Asia. Enjoy sundowner cocktails at La Plancha or Merah Putih beachside.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before departure — smoothies, yogurt parfait, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sardine Restaurant, Seminyak — elegant open-air dining beside a rice paddy, serving the freshest seafood with French and Balinese influences.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Merah Putih, Seminyak — stunning architectural space serving refined Indonesian cuisine with an extensive wine and cocktail list.

day_by_day.notes: Private transfer to and from Seminyak is recommended for comfort and flexibility. Confirm beach club reservations and sun lounger bookings in advance — they fill up quickly in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to East Bali — depart early by private car. Visit the majestic Pura Besakih (Mother Temple of Bali) on the slopes of Mount Agung — Bali's largest and most sacred temple complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Tirtagangga Water Palace — a royal garden and spring water complex featuring ornate fountains and stepping stones. Explore the surrounding traditional villages and terraced rice fields of East Bali.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Sidemen Valley on the return journey — one of Bali's most serene and undiscovered valleys with dramatic views of Mount Agung. Return to Ubud by early evening.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast — eggs your way, fresh tropical fruit, toast, and Balinese coffee before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium local restaurant in Karangasem/Tirtagangga — try bebek betutu (slow-cooked spiced duck) or fresh grilled fish with sambal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique, Ubud — indulge in the chef's tasting menu with full wine pairing for a memorable fine dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Besakih Temple requires a guide and sarong — both available at the entrance. Start early to avoid midday heat and crowds. The round trip from Ubud is approximately 3–4 hours of driving total.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Ashtanga yoga class at The Yoga Barn or a private session with a dedicated instructor arranged by the hotel. Follow with a Balinese traditional healer (Balian) consultation — a unique spiritual wellness experience unique to Bali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) — an ancient archaeological site and Hindu sanctuary near Ubud. Continue to Yeh Pulu — a 14th-century rock relief carving hidden among the rice fields, accessible via a scenic walk.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Gamelan music or Legong dance performance arranged exclusively for guests — many boutique stays in Ubud can organize intimate cultural performances in their gardens.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga breakfast at the hotel — acai bowls, smashed avocado, poached eggs, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Room4Dessert — a celebrated avant-garde dessert and savory tasting experience by chef Will Goldfarb, featured in Netflix's Chef's Table.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alaya Resort's Plantation rooftop — enjoy creative Indonesian cuisine with panoramic Ubud views and fine wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Balian (healer) consultation should be arranged through the hotel concierge and is a deeply personal experience — approach with respect and openness. Goa Gajah requires a sarong.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise visit to Pura Luhur Batukaru — one of Bali's nine directional temples, nestled in misty mountain rainforest on the slopes of Mount Batukaru. A deeply spiritual and atmospheric experience with very few tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jatiluwih UNESCO World Heritage Rice Terraces — the most expansive and breathtaking rice terrace landscape in Bali. Enjoy a guided walk through the terraces with a local expert explaining the ancient subak water system.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Enjoy a sunset spa ritual at the hotel — choose a 2-hour Balinese Royal Lulur treatment (traditional royal body scrub, floral bath, and massage), perfect for rejuvenation.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium warung overlooking Jatiluwih Terraces — enjoy nasi campur (Balinese mixed rice plate) with panoramic views of the UNESCO landscape.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Locavore NXT — the casual but equally innovative sibling of Locavore, offering a plant-forward menu with natural wines in a relaxed setting.

day_by_day.notes: Batukaru Temple is at higher altitude — bring a light jacket and arrive early for mist and atmospheric lighting. Jatiluwih charges a small entry fee. The drive from Ubud is approximately 1.5 hours each way.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga and pranayama (breathwork) session in a scenic outdoor setting — ideally at a rice terrace or jungle pavilion arranged by the hotel. Follow with a sound healing or crystal bowl meditation session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Half-day white water rafting on the Ayung River — Bali's most scenic rafting experience, passing through lush jungle gorges and past ancient stone carvings. Suitable for all fitness levels. Arrange premium operator (e.g., Mason Adventures) for top-tier equipment and guides.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-departure shopping in Ubud — browse premium galleries, boutique jewelry stores, and artisan shops along Jalan Raya Ubud for authentic Balinese keepsakes and luxury souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — full Balinese spread with lawar, sate lilit, black rice, fresh fruit, and Kintamani coffee.
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch at the rafting operator's riverside restaurant — fresh Balinese buffet with river views.
meals.dinner: Special dinner at Bridges Bali — cliff-edge dining with a curated 5-course dinner and sommelier-selected wine pairing to celebrate the penultimate evening.

day_by_day.notes: Rafting is best booked through the hotel concierge for premium service. Wear clothes you don't mind getting wet and bring a change of clothes. Ubud shopping is best in the late afternoon when light is golden.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning yoga session at The Yoga Barn — choose a class that resonates with your journey, such as a Heart-Opening Flow or Yoga Nidra (yogic sleep) for deep relaxation and integration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely farewell afternoon — return to a favorite Ubud spot for reflection, or visit the Neka Art Museum to appreciate Balinese and Indonesian fine art. Optional: final spa treatment or facial at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner — reserve a private dining experience in the hotel's garden or jungle pavilion, with a personalized menu crafted by the chef, floral décor, and a bottle of vintage Champagne to celebrate 13 days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory in-hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh tropical fruit tower, pastries, and premium Bali coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hujan Locale — a final taste of refined Indonesian regional cuisine in a beautifully designed space.
meals.dinner: Private in-villa or garden farewell dinner at Ubud Boutique Stay — 5-course personalized Balinese tasting menu with Champagne and wine pairing, served by a dedicated butler.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange checkout logistics and airport transfer for Day 13 with the hotel concierge today. Pack purchased souvenirs carefully. Confirm any remaining spa or activity bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise moment — sit on your private villa terrace with a cup of Kintamani coffee and soak in the sounds of the Balinese jungle one last time. Optional: a short 20-minute guided mindfulness walk through the hotel gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Ubud Boutique Stay. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport (allow at least 2.5 hours before departure). Enjoy a final Balinese treat at the airport's premium lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry with you the memories of 13 extraordinary days of beaches, yoga, culture, and world-class cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final in-hotel breakfast — light and nourishing: fresh tropical fruit, yogurt, granola, avocado toast, and freshly pressed green juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or airport premium lounge before departure.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer timing with the hotel the night before. Allow extra time at the airport for international departures — Ngurah Rai can be busy. Keep one carry-on bag accessible for any last-minute purchases. Selamat jalan — safe travels!
